title: Bounded Recovery Structures of Linear Codes: Transfer, Reliability, and Geometry
description: This preprint studies bounded local recovery at a distinguished coordinate of a represented linear code: all normalized dual recovery equations within a helper bound, their exact helper supports, the resulting recovery-set family, and helper-failure reliability. It proves that the minimum-weight recovery equations of an MDS code reconstruct the represented code, gives an exact weighted-functional transfer theorem for concatenation, and realizes every fixed represented bounded recovery structure satisfying the persistent confinement bound with positive density in an asymptotically good fixed-alphabet family. A structural sparse-paving construction gives two represented seeds with the same pointed-perspective data, repair count, locality, matching and transversal numbers, unique minimum-blocker count, and helper-degree multiset, but different bounded reliability and EXIT curves; one common outer family preserves the separation at positive density. The paper also develops deletion-contraction reliability and bounded-EXIT calculi. Twisted-cubic-axis and quartic-normal-rational-curve nucleus codes in characteristic three provide geometric applications, including a harmonic Steiner recovery structure.
